explanation: Biodiversity is not distributed uniformly across the Earth; it reaches its highest levels in tropical regions near the equator. Ecologists identify critical regions known as biodiversity hotspots. These hotspots contain a disproportionately large share of global biodiversity—harboring roughly 44% of all known higher plant species and 35% of terrestrial vertebrate species—despite occupying only 1.4% of the Earth's total land surface area.
